title: Double to integer: truncates; out of range raises or is NULL
description: A cast from `Float64` to an integer truncates toward zero (2.7 is 2, -2.7 is -2). A value out of the target's range, ±inf or NaN raises with `strict=True` (the default, `InvalidOperationError`) and is NULL with `strict=False`.
`wrap_numerical=True` saturates for doubles (1e19 is 127 in `Int8`, -1e19 is -128, NaN is 0, Rust's `as`), where it wraps for integers (polars-cast-int).
reference: `float_to_int: TRUNCATE` (#209); `cast_failure` as the cast states, `THROW_EXCEPTION` for `UNSPECIFIED`.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
